title: The Credit Card Side Hustle No One Talks About
channel: Chris Koerner on The Koerner Office Podcast
promo_conflict: Colin says bank credit-card affiliate links are a key revenue source and that a premium-card signup can pay about $400. His card recommendations may therefore be financially incentivized.

stated_problem.quote: I think the number one issue that I'm helping with, that people feel as I am leaving money on the table.
stated_problem.speaker: Colin Stroud

idea.name: Go Somewhere points strategy and trip planning
idea.one_liner: Advises business owners on earning more credit-card rewards and helps points holders find trips; earns from fixed service fees and card affiliate commissions.
idea.customer: Business owners with substantial card spend, plus people worldwide holding points they want to use for travel.
idea.offer: A one-time credit-card strategy consultation with written recommendations and follow-up support; a separate points-trip research and planning service.
idea.revenue_model: $875 one-time consulting package; trip planning typically $300-$400, with more complex work around $500-$600. The transcript later gives a $50 deposit and says the scope fee is between $2 and $500. Also earns bank-card affiliate commissions; the transcript does not give total affiliate revenue.

key_quotes.quote: And effectively, I'm a credit card rewards consultant.
That doesn't mean a lot to a lot of people, what I tell my grandma is that I am a travel agent for people with points.
One, helping business owners create credit card strategies for earn a ton of points.
Number two, I help people book trips with these points that they're sitting on.
Offer one is basically a business owner consulting package. I charge $875.
And then the second part of the business is simply just that trip planning portion.
Once it's booked, we charge a flat fee. That's typically three or $400.
So I'm posting one, two times a day, six days a week, and LinkedIn has been my best friend, for sure.
So this trip research service I've talked about, that is now 90% handled by two guys I hire, who are awesome points experts who do most of that work for me on behalf of the Go-Somewhere team
So once I started realizing that, that has become a key part of my revenue is sharing affiliate links to clients in my newsletter and even on social media.
So in terms of delivering that service, it's all done through AI by humans.

acquisition_channels.details: Organic LinkedIn content, typically one or two posts a day six days a week; he says clients arrive inbound. He also started posting on X, with little traction so far.

ideas.delivery: Colin conducts the strategy consultation, researches card options, writes recommendations, and supports implementation by email or text. Customers can submit a website form for trip research; Colin's two points-expert contractors now handle most of that research through a custom CRM and dashboard.

prices: $2-$500 scope fee as transcribed at L0297

ideas.other_uk_rules: UK GDPR applies to customer spending and travel data; PECR applies to newsletter marketing and requires the appropriate consent or soft opt-in and an unsubscribe route. Check FCA financial-promotion and credit-broking rules for card recommendations and affiliate links. Consumer-contract rules may apply to remote services; arranging or booking travel could bring additional travel rules into scope.
